proposal.title: Consolidate NCC 1979 execution into the campaign and feature ecosystem pioneers
proposal.reason: Start development on 9 January 1979. Retire the redundant campaign-execution process and discard its inputs/outcomes as instructed. Merge its unique actions into concise campaign steps; move all five step-owned and two boundary-owned events directly to campaign marketing_steps, keeping one owner and all product launch links. Replace overlapping presentation/guide prose with a 54-minute programme that covers the approved Apple/S-100 profiles, ROM TUI/video, FlexiDisk II transfer and AION C 2.0. Feature SSG as an existing C/TUI pioneer and date the Tandy, Centronics, Epson, Leedex and Sanyo examples accurately; future offerings remain prospective, not June shipments or confirmed commitments.

before.title: NCC 1979 development and open-architecture programme
before.description: From 26 July 1978, prepare the products, technical cooperation and open-architecture programme associated with NCC 1979. Include limited Apple cooperation, the combined NCC presentation and Apple II/S-100 expansion launch through the existing NCC 1979 campaign execution with its recorded follow-up through 14 January 1980. The programme includes AION C IDE 2.0, its native Apple II backend/runtime and cross-platform disk-transfer acceptance.

participant.role: C platform, software and migration contributor
limited documentation and compatibility assistance partner

inputs.description: The Aurelia launch establishes the working platform, peripherals and software on which wider compatibility products and the next NCC programme build.

steps.description: Agree limited Apple technical cooperation on 8 February 1979, obtaining documentation, test equipment and compatibility assistance for native Apple expansion products.

Continue Logix-funded native Apple expansion development and compatibility testing, allowing independent compatible products. Apple retains its own peripheral strategy, does not manufacture FlexiBUS devices and does not adopt FlexiBUS as an official standard.

Before the 4 June 1979 presentation, develop and integrate the Aurelia-hosted AION C 2.0 6502 backend, Apple runtime/native-hardware libraries, ROM-backed video-card TUI and Apple-format FlexiDisk II export. Exercise shared API conformance, native Apple calls, bank/keyboard/memory limits and end-to-end build/write/run acceptance.
Execute campaign.ncc1979 through its existing campaign execution process, including preparation, NCC presentations and recorded follow-up.
Coordinate the marketing campaign: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign.

outcomes.description: Apple II and S-100 expansion products have a recorded launch, and the campaign has presented documented compatibility and migration options with follow-up. Partner invitations and adoption targets remain distinct from signed commitments and measured results.
Limited Apple compatibility cooperation supports the native expansion work without committing Apple to manufacture FlexiBUS devices or adopt the Logix platform.

Supply the AION C IDE 2.0 cross-development edition and its documented native Apple target and disk-export tools for the NCC launch. The technical definition retains explicit image-fit and interoperability acceptance requirements; no unrecorded performance measurements are asserted.

after.title: NCC 1979 development and open-architecture programme

The directly owned marketing campaign covers preparation, the June presentation and follow-up through 14 January 1980.

before.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
before.objective: Encourage independent manufacturers and developers to adopt documented compatibility interfaces, and show customers how supported software, documents and peripherals can protect their investment across computer brands.
message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
Use documented interfaces and qualified configurations to connect products from independent suppliers.
Choose CP/M applications, FlexiBUS peripherals and display options separately; adopting one does not require the entire Logix platform.
Prepare for future computers through portable C source and documented interfaces while continuing to use and support established eight-bit systems.
audience: Business customers choosing computers, applications and peripherals.
Independent computer and peripheral manufacturers evaluating compatibility programmes.
Software publishers, developers, dealers and integrators supporting existing and future systems.

marketing_steps.description: Qualify partner claims and protect the next-generation architecture disclosure.

marketing_presentation.description: Identify shipping products, qualified configurations, prototypes and plans separately. Manufacturer interest and campaign targets are not signed agreements, verified adoption or sales.

CP/M remains commercially licensed. Non-exclusive implementation rights do not change software ownership or imply open-source licensing. Reference-code rights, certification scope and support terms must be stated before making firm offers.
Claim compatibility only for named software versions, resources, host adapters and tested configurations. Preserve each supplier’s brand, licences and support responsibilities.
Label the Model II demonstration as a prototype until customer release. AION supplies the June 1979 cards; SMC remains a future source subject to individual chip qualification.

Apple’s demonstration participation covers native Apple II products and does not endorse S-100 systems. These products provide neither Apple CP/M/Z80 execution nor automatic conversion of existing Apple graphics.

Until 19 May 1980, refer to future systems only as next-generation computers. Withhold product, processor and OS names; word size, ISA, registers, execution design, address and memory organisation; performance figures, clock rates, chip counts, schematics, board images, bus topology and future display specifications.

Keep coprocessor implementation and integration details, unreleased next-generation-target SDKs, compiler output, binaries and revealing benchmarks confidential. Apply this embargo to presentations, questions, advertising, dealer scripts, sales proposals, OEM briefings, clinics and all attachments; current CP/M, FlexiBUS and optional display documentation may be shared. The released Apple II 6502 target and its June 1979 documentation may be demonstrated publicly.

Use released eight-bit software and explicitly identified qualified prototypes in demonstrations. Label prepared data and recordings, obtain partner clearance, and report measured resource and interoperability limits rather than implying universal performance.
Do not imply an engineering guarantee, product withdrawal date or promise that every model remains in production. Do not promise funded support for an unspecified duration.

marketing_steps.description: Demonstrate independent customer choices at NCC 1979.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {programme_minutes} minutes for the presentation programme; questions and follow-up are separate.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Explain how independent software, peripheral and display choices can protect a customer’s investment.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Demonstrate an Abacus document round trip between Aurelia and the Model II prototype using separately qualified host editions. Show supported common behaviour without promising identical binaries or disk formats.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Demonstrate Abacus, then independent SSG General Ledger records and summary export. Explain the prepared data and separate licensing; do not imply that SSG has a Model II port.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Operate a qualified peripheral sequentially on named hosts. Show identification, driver support and supported application functions, attaching only when the port is quiescent.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Present the five Apple II/S-100 expansion products with the Apple representative. Demonstrate {compiler}: build a small shared C sample on Aurelia, write an Apple-format executable disk with {disk}, move it to Apple II and run the native 6502 result. Show the same frames, controls and graphics through {video}, then a separate example using native Apple graphics and speaker functions. Explain the optional FlexiBUS interface, required compatible monitor and qualified S-100 CP/M/TUI path. Apple participation does not endorse S-100 systems.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. DRI, Tandy, Microsoft, SSG management and confirmed peripheral participants explain their responsibilities and commercial access. Distinguish current AION chip supply from prospective SMC supply and signed partners from recruitment prospects.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. {presenter} explains that future computers will not run existing Z80 binaries natively. Existing C tools and documented APIs reduce source migration work; recompilation, adaptation and testing remain necessary. Describe the planned optional Z80 coprocessor and the continuing role of eight-bit systems without revealing the new architecture.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Identify available products, prototypes and future plans. Direct customers and developers to documented configurations, licence terms, the compatibility directory and programme registration.

marketing_steps.description: Explain the separate software, peripheral and display compatibility profiles.

marketing_presentation.description: Specify the CP/M core and optional extension versions, processor instruction set, available transient-program memory, adapters and qualified applications for each configuration. Document common file formats and APIs. FlexiBUS and Logix video are optional; native displays, disks and conventional ports remain valid. Ordinary CP/M support does not guarantee every extended application, Z80 binary, file system or floppy format.

Publish electrical and transport rules, device-class profiles, host drivers, diagnostics and named qualification results. Other processors and operating systems may use their own drivers without adopting CP/M or Logix video. Device identification alone does not prove feature compatibility. Version 1 uses one device per point-to-point port, with no passive hub or daisy chain; its faster rate allows at most 50 KB/s before protocol overhead.

Separate graphics API compatibility from controller cards, the digital monitor link and qualified display modes. FlexiBUS and the full Aurelia architecture are optional. An 80-column mode needs a qualified 640-pixel monitor; adding a card does not give existing 320-pixel launch monitors that resolution.

The NCC launch covers the Apple II Expansion Card, FlexiDisk II, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. The Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II are existing products presented alongside the three new interface/video cards. Cards initially use AION chips and include native Apple drivers and examples or supported S-100 CP/M adapters as appropriate. Keep host requirements and supplier support explicit. AION C IDE 2.0 runs on Aurelia and cross-compiles native Apple II programs. Both video cards implement the full contemporary Aurelia TUI and graphics profile with ROM and libraries; S-100 TUI requires qualified CP/M extensions. Apple-native graphics, sound and hardware remain available through target-specific functions.
Explain implementation and qualification requirements for {subject}.
Explain supported interaction behaviour under {subject}.
Present {subject} to developers implementing supported interfaces.
Explain source portability through {subject}, with recompilation and testing still required.
Distinguish graphics API compatibility under {subject} from qualified display hardware.
Explain the qualified monitor connection defined by {subject}; this is not a consumer television interface.

marketing_steps.description: Recruit independent implementers under explicit terms and governance.

marketing_presentation.description: Describe DRI’s software leadership and Logix’s hardware contribution. Invite independent computer, peripheral and software suppliers to a programme offering published specifications, versioning, backward-support policies, reference drivers, conformance tests, configuration diagnostics and a certification dispute process. Explain non-exclusive own-brand implementation, equal access to qualified components, disclosed supply priorities and manufacturer representation in a working group.

Identify the unresolved licence terms, reference-code redistribution rights, support duration and staffing, legacy-maintenance budget, working-group charter and voting rules, certification operator and scope, supply allocations, lead times and warranties. Present these as matters to settle, not existing contractual guarantees.

Invite suppliers to offer wider carriage, letter-quality printing, specialist forms and faster devices. Require the relevant status, character or graphics, paper and form-control support; the basic printer protocol does not cover every feature.
Invite business-chart and engineering-output devices, subject to a new plotting profile and suitable application support.
Invite communications and remote-access products with defined serial data, flow-control, modem-status and control profiles and host drivers.

Invite larger floppy systems, backup products and selected hard disks. Specify geometry, removable-media errors, durable writes, boot rules and measured throughput. Native faster disk controllers remain a valid choice.
Invite instruments, readers and business-input devices with published class or vendor-extension profiles and host drivers. Do not imply that foreign-processor ROM drivers execute automatically.

marketing_steps.description: Explain source migration, legacy support and the continuing eight-bit market.

marketing_presentation.description: The 4 June 1979 announcement explains source migration and the planned optional Z80 compatibility path. Full architecture disclosure is scheduled for 19 May 1980. The all-years technical catalogue is internal author material, not a 1979 press kit.

Use the established Z80 C environment, documented APIs, portable file formats and separate platform adapters. A later target needs recompilation and testing, with review of assembly code, integer and pointer assumptions, memory banking and direct hardware access. Source portability does not preserve native Z80 binary execution. The June 1979 release also targets native Apple II 6502 code, with Apple DOS 3.2-compatible output disks written on Aurelia through FlexiDisk II. Common console/file code and Logix video API calls minimize source changes; Apple/Aurelia-specific functions remain explicit adapters.

Describe an optional Z80 coprocessor planned for qualified legacy applications. Availability and compatibility are not guaranteed for every model or hardware-dependent program. Keep its implementation, interconnect, memory mapping and host integration confidential until the architecture reveal.
Maintain CP/M tools and applications alongside next-generation development. Publish a funded support duration before making a dated service promise.
Explain that eight-bit computers retain useful business roles while falling costs broaden home, education and personal use. There is no fixed date when all business customers switch platforms.

The current professional digital monitor interface cannot drive a consumer television. A computer intended to use an existing television requires separate display engineering; the basic-storage configuration remains unresolved.

marketing_steps.description: Prepare the actual transfer demonstration, venue and architecture answers.

marketing_presentation.description: Document the actual file-transfer route and floppy formats used for the Aurelia-to-Model-II round trip. Publish tested RAM and application-workspace requirements, load and recalculation times and document-capacity limits. Label prepared data and recordings and preserve independent SSG branding and participant clearances.
Use booked presentation space; main-stage access, the exact slot and audiovisual suitability require confirmation. The eight presentation stages total 54 minutes, followed by questions.

Use this response to questions seeking confidential details: We will discuss the new architecture at NCC 1980. Today we can describe our C migration approach and planned optional Z80 compatibility path.

marketing_steps.description: Evaluate manufacturer adoption against stated targets.

marketing_presentation.description: By the end of 1979, aim for Tandy shipping, one additional OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension or FlexiBUS configuration, another in qualification and verified third-party devices in several categories. By NCC 1980, aim for three to five distinct non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations. Count Tandy once and exclude duplicate dealer builds and product variants; these are targets, not achieved results.

after.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
after.objective: Demonstrate portable C applications and compatible peripherals and displays across computer brands, introduce the June 1979 Apple II/S-100 offerings, and recruit independent implementers through dated qualification and follow-up.
message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
Build on Aurelia, run native code on Apple II, and retain familiar interaction with Logix video.
Independent software, peripherals and displays can adopt shared standards without adopting the whole Logix platform.
audience: Business customers choosing computers, applications and peripherals.
Independent computer and peripheral manufacturers evaluating compatibility programmes.
Software publishers, developers, dealers and integrators supporting existing and future systems.

marketing_steps.description: Recruit independent computer, software and peripheral implementers.

marketing_presentation.description: Logix coordinates outreach, AION supports software and application integration, and DRI supports CP/M qualification. Prioritise North Star, with Lifeboat as a possible integration/distribution partner, then Vector Graphic. Both are strong CP/M prospects; FlexiBUS is a moderately strong fit, while Logix video is a moderate fit for North Star and a lower fit for Vector. Existing applications and display investment shape each proposal; outreach does not establish an agreement.

Cromemco is a moderate CP/M/FlexiBUS prospect but a weak Logix-video prospect because of its independent OS and graphics strategy. Altos is a moderately strong CP/M prospect with moderate FlexiBUS and limited video potential. Intertec has moderately strong CP/M and moderate host-specific FlexiBUS potential; schedule late-1979 evaluation and possible 1980 qualification. Heath/Heathkit is a moderate CP/M/FlexiBUS prospect for later feasibility work. Neither implies a June release or a host redesign.

Seek independent implementations in printers, disks, communications, input, instruments and specialist output. Match opportunities to vendor-owned product variants rather than relabelling every existing device. Printing needs explicit character/status and paper handling; plotting and specialist functions need their own profiles, while disks need geometry, durable writes, boot and recovery rules. Native faster disk interfaces remain valid.

marketing_steps.description: Publish separate compatibility profiles and update them for the June offerings.

marketing_presentation.description: Publish {cpm} host/CPU, memory and adapter requirements alongside DRI’s portable-extension release. Ordinary CP/M remains usable without TUI or FlexiBUS; extended services and application binaries require named supported configurations. Explain {tui} as shared interaction and {c} as source-level contracts with separate target builds. The Apple II/S-100 profiles and AION C 2.0 arrive at the June launch; later ERA and pointer capabilities are outside this release.

Publish {bus} electrical/transport rules, host drivers, device classes and diagnostics independently of CP/M and video. One device connects to each point-to-point port; passive hubs and daisy chains are unsupported, and the faster rate is at most {rate} KB/s before overhead. Distinguish the C display API, video controller and {video} monitor connection. Eighty columns require a qualified 640-pixel monitor; a consumer TV or existing 320-pixel monitor does not become compatible through a cable.

Provide {sdk}, published versions, reference-driver access, conformance tests, configuration diagnostics and a certification dispute process. State non-exclusive own-brand implementation and component-access principles, supply priorities and manufacturer participation. Settle reference-code rights, CP/M licensing, support duration/staffing, maintenance funding, governance, certification scope, allocations and warranties before firm offers. Preserve each supplier’s ownership, branding and specialist support.

marketing_steps.description: Qualify the demonstrations, supplier contributions and public disclosure.

marketing_presentation.description: Rehearse named configurations with supplier workshops and record failures and corrections. Test the Aurelia/Model II document round trip separately from Aurelia compilation, FlexiDisk II Apple-format writing and Apple II execution. Measure memory/workspace, disk formats, loading/recalculation, UI redraw and peripheral behaviour; test ROM-bank restoration across display/disk calls. Book suitable space and audiovisual equipment, secure participant clearance and label prepared data or recordings.

Keep the Model II demonstration labelled prototype until its release. AION supplies the June cards; SMC is a future source subject to chip qualification. Apple’s participation concerns native Apple products, not S-100 endorsement. Separate shipping products, qualified demonstrations, prototypes and recruitment prospects; manufacturer interest, forecasts and targets are not sales or commitments.

Until {reveal}, describe the new architecture only as next-generation computers. Withhold product/processor/OS names, word size, ISA/registers, memory organization, clocks, performance figures, chip counts, schematics, board images, bus topology, future displays and coprocessor internals. Apply this to talks, Q&A, press, dealers, OEMs and attachments. Current CP/M/FlexiBUS/video documentation and the released Apple 6502 target are public. Answer architecture questions with the NCC 1980 disclosure plan; make no unspecified support-duration, withdrawal or engineering guarantee.

marketing_steps.description: Present cross-platform C development, familiar interfaces and the independent ecosystem.

marketing_presentation.description: The presentation lasts {programme_minutes} minutes, followed by questions. Show current products first and label the supplier roadmap separately.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Open with independent choice: shared application interfaces, documents and peripherals let customers keep useful work while changing computer brands. Introduce the software, bus and display standards as independently adoptable.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. DRI explains the portable CP/M extensions. Demonstrate an Abacus document round trip between Aurelia and the {model} prototype using separately qualified editions and an explicit transfer path. Show the {option} as a prototype; its recorded release is {release}, not the NCC date.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Feature {ledger} as an independent C-application pioneer. SSG demonstrates its native Z80 AION C implementation, ROM TUI forms and versioned balance exports to Abacus, explaining the benefit of shared editing and controls while retaining its accounting rules, ownership and support. This is General Ledger, not a larger accounting suite, a Model II port or a newly released Apple edition. Show how {basic} also uses shared TUI services without describing BASIC as a C port.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Operate a qualified FlexiBUS peripheral sequentially on named hosts. Show identification, supported class functions and driver requirements, attaching only with the port quiescent. Introduce the Apple II Expansion Card, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface and dual-format FlexiDisk II as separate choices.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Present {apple_video} and {s100_video} with ROM-backed TUI and callable libraries. On matching qualified monitors, demonstrate the full June 1979 Aurelia control behaviour and text/bitmap/sprite modes: frames, windows, editing, selection and redraw. Apple uses native 6502 code; S-100 TUI requires qualified CP/M/TUI extensions. Explain keyboard-command mappings and independent host performance. Preserve native Apple graphics/sound access; no automatic conversion of legacy graphics or later mouse/professional modes is implied.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Launch {compiler}: edit and compile a small shared C sample on Aurelia, save the native 6502 executable on an Apple DOS 3.2-compatible disk using {disk}, move the disk to Apple II and run it under its existing DOS installation. A compatible Disk II reader needs no Logix interface merely to read the disk; directly connecting FlexiDisk II to Apple does. Rebuild common TUI/drawing calls for Logix video, then show separately named native Apple graphics and speaker functions. The IDE stays on Aurelia; CPU-specific assembly and direct hardware access still need adapters. An Apple representative joins this native Apple demonstration without endorsing S-100 systems.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Give independent hardware pioneers a dedicated roadmap segment. Use {bridge} and {printer} to explain vendor-owned FlexiBUS bridge/native-interface approaches, and {leedex} and {sanyo} to explain purpose-built digital-input monitor variants. These are candidate paths in June, not shipping products or confirmed stage participants: the recorded estimated releases are {bridge_date}, {printer_date}, {leedex_date} and {sanyo_date}, respectively. Native Centronics printers remain behind a bridge; existing composite monitors do not become digital through a cable. Describe only tested raster/readability profiles, without promising 80 columns on every monitor. Invite supplier representatives only once participation and claims are cleared.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. {presenter} explains that shared C logic and documented APIs reduce migration work, while target-specific builds, data-format validation and testing remain necessary. Future computers will not execute Z80 binaries natively; describe the planned optional Z80 compatibility path without revealing its implementation. Continue CP/M tools and maintenance alongside future development; eight-bit systems retain business, home and education roles without a fixed replacement date.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Close with available products, prototype demonstrations and prospective supplier programmes clearly distinguished. Direct customers to dealer demonstrations and developers to the SDK, compatibility directory, migration clinics and implementation programme.

marketing_steps.description: Run dealer demonstrations, trade-press activity and developer clinics.

marketing_presentation.description: Reuse the NCC demonstrations and compatibility guides rather than repeat the keynote. Teach C target adapters, console/file portability, the Apple disk-transfer workflow, ROM TUI bindings and device-class drivers. Publish named supported configurations, application editions, test failures and support contacts; distinguish shipping products, prototypes and qualification work.

Refresh the pioneer directory as products become available. The Model II CP/M/FlexiBUS release is {tandy_date}; the {bridge} has an estimated {bridge_date} release. Later printer and monitor candidates stay on the roadmap until their own dates and qualification evidence. Suppliers retain their own brands, licences, sales and support.

marketing_steps.description: Review adoption targets and the evidence behind ecosystem growth.

marketing_presentation.description: By end-1979, target Tandy shipping, one additional OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension or FlexiBUS configuration, another in qualification and verified devices in several categories. By NCC 1980, target {manufacturers} distinct non-Logix manufacturers. Count Tandy once; exclude duplicate dealer builds and SKUs. These are goals, not achieved totals.

Track compatible-computer sell-through, qualified C and other application editions, peripheral shipments/classes, document interchange, support incidents, supplier concentration and component availability. Compare each pioneer’s actual scope and release date with the directory; separate application use of an API, bus implementation and digital-monitor compatibility. Do not turn adoption assumptions into measured sales.

marketing_steps.description: Publish customer evidence and prepare the next campaign.

marketing_presentation.description: Assemble verified customer examples, compatibility results and supplier configurations. Report progress and unresolved access/support issues, keeping future releases and NCC 1980 targets separate from results. The {printer} is recorded only to {release_month}; do not infer shipment by this January review from month precision alone. Leedex and Sanyo digital variants remain later roadmap items. Maintain the architecture embargo until the announced reveal.

before.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign — execution
before.description: Prepare the compatibility programme and partner demonstrations, deliver the NCC 1979 presentation and expansion-product launch, then run recruitment, dealer activity and qualification follow-up through the January 1980 review. Campaign.ncc1979 supplies the messages, presentation and marketing materials.

inputs.description: The Aurelia launch provides the working platform and business applications used to prepare cross-vendor demonstrations.
The Tandy cooperation agreement provides the basis for the Model II prototype and application-interchange work.
The limited Apple cooperation agreement provides documentation, test machines and compatibility assistance for native Apple II products.

Prepare named configurations, host-specific drivers, documented transfer paths and measured resource limits. Protect future architecture information and clear partner participation before public demonstrations.

outcomes.description: Published compatibility profiles, implementation guidance and records of unresolved access and support terms.
Rehearsed demonstration configurations, interoperability test records and an issue register distinguishing verified behaviour from limitations.
The NCC presentation and expansion-product launch have been delivered, with native Apple and S-100 support described separately and partner responsibilities retained.

An updated compatibility directory, recruitment and qualification records, dealer and developer materials, and an evidence-based closing review. Adoption and sales targets are not treated as achieved outcomes.

steps.description: Evaluate recruitment prospects and engineering kits. Prioritise North Star, with Lifeboat as a possible integration or distribution partner, then Vector Graphic. Preserve existing applications and display investment; interest does not constitute an agreement.

Treat North Star and Vector as strong CP/M prospects with moderately strong FlexiBUS prospects; optional Logix video is a moderate fit for North Star and a lower fit for Vector. Cromemco is a moderate CP/M and FlexiBUS prospect but a weak Logix-video prospect because of its own OS and graphics strategy. Altos is a moderately strong CP/M prospect with moderate FlexiBUS and limited Logix-video potential; no platform redesign is assumed. Intertec has moderately strong CP/M and moderate host-specific FlexiBUS potential, with limited Logix-video interest; plan late-1979 evaluation and possible 1980 qualification, not June availability. Heath/Heathkit has moderate CP/M and host-specific FlexiBUS potential but limited Logix-video interest; treat it as later feasibility work, not a promised 1979 release. These assessments guide outreach and do not establish commitments.
Publish compatibility profiles and provide reference-driver and test access alongside the separate DRI extension release. Record unresolved commercial and support terms.

Prepare the presentation space, audiovisual equipment and qualified demonstration systems. Test document round trips, disk formats, memory limits, loading, recalculation and device behaviour. Review all public material for the embargo and secure partner clearance.
Run supplier workshops, test named configurations and record failures and required corrections before public demonstrations.
Deliver the NCC presentation and the combined Apple II/S-100 expansion-product launch using the approved campaign materials and qualified systems.
Run dealer demonstrations, joint trade-press activity and developer clinics. Maintain a directory that distinguishes shipping, qualified and prototype configurations.
Review progress against the campaign’s adoption targets using verified OEM configurations, qualifications and third-party device availability.

Track compatible-computer sell-through across vendors, qualified application editions, peripheral shipments and supported device classes, document-interchange results, support incidents, supplier concentration and component availability. Count distinct manufacturers rather than duplicate dealer builds or SKUs.

Prepare the closing review with verified customer examples, compatibility results and partner configurations. Report progress toward NCC 1980 goals without claiming unverified results or disclosing future architecture.

Exercise shared API conformance, native Apple calls, bank/keyboard/memory limits and end-to-end build/write/run acceptance.
Run the NCC 1979 campaign, including supplier briefings, compatibility profiles, workshops, the product presentation, roadshows and adoption reviews.

outcomes.description: Apple II and S-100 expansion products have a recorded launch, and the campaign has presented documented compatibility and migration options with follow-up. Partner invitations and adoption targets remain distinct from signed commitments and measured results.
Limited Apple compatibility cooperation supports the native expansion work without committing Apple to manufacture FlexiBUS devices or adopt the Logix platform.

Supply the AION C IDE 2.0 cross-development edition and its documented native Apple target and disk-export tools for the NCC launch. The technical definition retains explicit image-fit and interoperability acceptance requirements; no unrecorded performance measurements are asserted.

before.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
before.objective: Encourage independent manufacturers and developers to adopt documented compatibility interfaces, and show customers how supported software, documents and peripherals can protect their investment across computer brands.
message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
Use documented interfaces and qualified configurations to connect products from independent suppliers.
Choose CP/M applications, FlexiBUS peripherals and display options separately; adopting one does not require the entire Logix platform.
Prepare for future computers through portable C source and documented interfaces while continuing to use and support established eight-bit systems.
audience: Business customers choosing computers, applications and peripherals.
Independent computer and peripheral manufacturers evaluating compatibility programmes.
Software publishers, developers, dealers and integrators supporting existing and future systems.

marketing_steps.description: Qualify partner claims and protect the next-generation architecture disclosure.

marketing_presentation.description: Identify shipping products, qualified configurations, prototypes and plans separately. Manufacturer interest and campaign targets are not signed agreements, verified adoption or sales.

CP/M remains commercially licensed. Non-exclusive implementation rights do not change software ownership or imply open-source licensing. Reference-code rights, certification scope and support terms must be stated before making firm offers.
Claim compatibility only for named software versions, resources, host adapters and tested configurations. Preserve each supplier’s brand, licences and support responsibilities.
Label the Model II demonstration as a prototype until customer release. AION supplies the June 1979 cards; SMC remains a future source subject to individual chip qualification.

Apple’s demonstration participation covers native Apple II products and does not endorse S-100 systems. These products provide neither Apple CP/M/Z80 execution nor automatic conversion of existing Apple graphics.

Until 19 May 1980, refer to future systems only as next-generation computers. Withhold product, processor and OS names; word size, ISA, registers, execution design, address and memory organisation; performance figures, clock rates, chip counts, schematics, board images, bus topology and future display specifications.

Keep coprocessor implementation and integration details, unreleased next-generation-target SDKs, compiler output, binaries and revealing benchmarks confidential. Apply this embargo to presentations, questions, advertising, dealer scripts, sales proposals, OEM briefings, clinics and all attachments; current CP/M, FlexiBUS and optional display documentation may be shared. The released Apple II 6502 target and its June 1979 documentation may be demonstrated publicly.

Use released eight-bit software and explicitly identified qualified prototypes in demonstrations. Label prepared data and recordings, obtain partner clearance, and report measured resource and interoperability limits rather than implying universal performance.
Do not imply an engineering guarantee, product withdrawal date or promise that every model remains in production. Do not promise funded support for an unspecified duration.

marketing_steps.description: Demonstrate independent customer choices at NCC 1979.

marketing_presentation.description: Allow {programme_minutes} minutes for the presentation programme; questions and follow-up are separate.
Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Explain how independent software, peripheral and display choices can protect a customer’s investment.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Demonstrate an Abacus document round trip between Aurelia and the Model II prototype using separately qualified host editions. Show supported common behaviour without promising identical binaries or disk formats.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Demonstrate Abacus, then independent SSG General Ledger records and summary export. Explain the prepared data and separate licensing; do not imply that SSG has a Model II port.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Operate a qualified peripheral sequentially on named hosts. Show identification, driver support and supported application functions, attaching only when the port is quiescent.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Present the five Apple II/S-100 expansion products with the Apple representative. Demonstrate {compiler}: build a small shared C sample on Aurelia, write an Apple-format executable disk with {disk}, move it to Apple II and run the native 6502 result. Show the same frames, controls and graphics through {video}, then a separate example using native Apple graphics and speaker functions. Explain the optional FlexiBUS interface, required compatible monitor and qualified S-100 CP/M/TUI path. Apple participation does not endorse S-100 systems.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. DRI, Tandy, Microsoft, SSG management and confirmed peripheral participants explain their responsibilities and commercial access. Distinguish current AION chip supply from prospective SMC supply and signed partners from recruitment prospects.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. {presenter} explains that future computers will not run existing Z80 binaries natively. Existing C tools and documented APIs reduce source migration work; recompilation, adaptation and testing remain necessary. Describe the planned optional Z80 coprocessor and the continuing role of eight-bit systems without revealing the new architecture.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes for this block. Identify available products, prototypes and future plans. Direct customers and developers to documented configurations, licence terms, the compatibility directory and programme registration.

marketing_steps.description: Explain the separate software, peripheral and display compatibility profiles.

marketing_presentation.description: Specify the CP/M core and optional extension versions, processor instruction set, available transient-program memory, adapters and qualified applications for each configuration. Document common file formats and APIs. FlexiBUS and Logix video are optional; native displays, disks and conventional ports remain valid. Ordinary CP/M support does not guarantee every extended application, Z80 binary, file system or floppy format.

Publish electrical and transport rules, device-class profiles, host drivers, diagnostics and named qualification results. Other processors and operating systems may use their own drivers without adopting CP/M or Logix video. Device identification alone does not prove feature compatibility. Version 1 uses one device per point-to-point port, with no passive hub or daisy chain; its faster rate allows at most 50 KB/s before protocol overhead.

Separate graphics API compatibility from controller cards, the digital monitor link and qualified display modes. FlexiBUS and the full Aurelia architecture are optional. An 80-column mode needs a qualified 640-pixel monitor; adding a card does not give existing 320-pixel launch monitors that resolution.

The NCC launch covers the Apple II Expansion Card, FlexiDisk II, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface, Apple II Video Card and S-100 Video Card. The Apple II Expansion Card and FlexiDisk II are existing products presented alongside the three new interface/video cards. Cards initially use AION chips and include native Apple drivers and examples or supported S-100 CP/M adapters as appropriate. Keep host requirements and supplier support explicit. AION C IDE 2.0 runs on Aurelia and cross-compiles native Apple II programs. Both video cards implement the full contemporary Aurelia TUI and graphics profile with ROM and libraries; S-100 TUI requires qualified CP/M extensions. Apple-native graphics, sound and hardware remain available through target-specific functions.
Explain implementation and qualification requirements for {subject}.
Explain supported interaction behaviour under {subject}.
Present {subject} to developers implementing supported interfaces.
Explain source portability through {subject}, with recompilation and testing still required.
Distinguish graphics API compatibility under {subject} from qualified display hardware.
Explain the qualified monitor connection defined by {subject}; this is not a consumer television interface.

marketing_steps.description: Recruit independent implementers under explicit terms and governance.

marketing_presentation.description: Describe DRI’s software leadership and Logix’s hardware contribution. Invite independent computer, peripheral and software suppliers to a programme offering published specifications, versioning, backward-support policies, reference drivers, conformance tests, configuration diagnostics and a certification dispute process. Explain non-exclusive own-brand implementation, equal access to qualified components, disclosed supply priorities and manufacturer representation in a working group.

Identify the unresolved licence terms, reference-code redistribution rights, support duration and staffing, legacy-maintenance budget, working-group charter and voting rules, certification operator and scope, supply allocations, lead times and warranties. Present these as matters to settle, not existing contractual guarantees.

Invite suppliers to offer wider carriage, letter-quality printing, specialist forms and faster devices. Require the relevant status, character or graphics, paper and form-control support; the basic printer protocol does not cover every feature.
Invite business-chart and engineering-output devices, subject to a new plotting profile and suitable application support.
Invite communications and remote-access products with defined serial data, flow-control, modem-status and control profiles and host drivers.

Invite larger floppy systems, backup products and selected hard disks. Specify geometry, removable-media errors, durable writes, boot rules and measured throughput. Native faster disk controllers remain a valid choice.
Invite instruments, readers and business-input devices with published class or vendor-extension profiles and host drivers. Do not imply that foreign-processor ROM drivers execute automatically.

marketing_steps.description: Explain source migration, legacy support and the continuing eight-bit market.

marketing_presentation.description: The 4 June 1979 announcement explains source migration and the planned optional Z80 compatibility path. Full architecture disclosure is scheduled for 19 May 1980. The all-years technical catalogue is internal author material, not a 1979 press kit.

Use the established Z80 C environment, documented APIs, portable file formats and separate platform adapters. A later target needs recompilation and testing, with review of assembly code, integer and pointer assumptions, memory banking and direct hardware access. Source portability does not preserve native Z80 binary execution. The June 1979 release also targets native Apple II 6502 code, with Apple DOS 3.2-compatible output disks written on Aurelia through FlexiDisk II. Common console/file code and Logix video API calls minimize source changes; Apple/Aurelia-specific functions remain explicit adapters.

Describe an optional Z80 coprocessor planned for qualified legacy applications. Availability and compatibility are not guaranteed for every model or hardware-dependent program. Keep its implementation, interconnect, memory mapping and host integration confidential until the architecture reveal.
Maintain CP/M tools and applications alongside next-generation development. Publish a funded support duration before making a dated service promise.
Explain that eight-bit computers retain useful business roles while falling costs broaden home, education and personal use. There is no fixed date when all business customers switch platforms.

The current professional digital monitor interface cannot drive a consumer television. A computer intended to use an existing television requires separate display engineering; the basic-storage configuration remains unresolved.

marketing_steps.description: Prepare the actual transfer demonstration, venue and architecture answers.

marketing_presentation.description: Document the actual file-transfer route and floppy formats used for the Aurelia-to-Model-II round trip. Publish tested RAM and application-workspace requirements, load and recalculation times and document-capacity limits. Label prepared data and recordings and preserve independent SSG branding and participant clearances.
Use booked presentation space; main-stage access, the exact slot and audiovisual suitability require confirmation. The eight presentation stages total 54 minutes, followed by questions.

Use this response to questions seeking confidential details: We will discuss the new architecture at NCC 1980. Today we can describe our C migration approach and planned optional Z80 compatibility path.

marketing_steps.description: Evaluate manufacturer adoption against stated targets.

marketing_presentation.description: By the end of 1979, aim for Tandy shipping, one additional OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension or FlexiBUS configuration, another in qualification and verified third-party devices in several categories. By NCC 1980, aim for three to five distinct non-Logix manufacturers with supported configurations. Count Tandy once and exclude duplicate dealer builds and product variants; these are targets, not achieved results.

after.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign
after.objective: Demonstrate portable C applications and compatible peripherals and displays across computer brands, introduce the June 1979 Apple II/S-100 offerings, and recruit independent implementers through dated qualification and follow-up.
message: Choose your computer. Keep your investment.
Build on Aurelia, run native code on Apple II, and retain familiar interaction with Logix video.
Independent software, peripherals and displays can adopt shared standards without adopting the whole Logix platform.
audience: Business customers choosing computers, applications and peripherals.
Independent computer and peripheral manufacturers evaluating compatibility programmes.
Software publishers, developers, dealers and integrators supporting existing and future systems.

marketing_steps.description: Recruit independent computer, software and peripheral implementers.

marketing_presentation.description: Logix coordinates outreach, AION supports software and application integration, and DRI supports CP/M qualification. Prioritise North Star, with Lifeboat as a possible integration/distribution partner, then Vector Graphic. Both are strong CP/M prospects; FlexiBUS is a moderately strong fit, while Logix video is a moderate fit for North Star and a lower fit for Vector. Existing applications and display investment shape each proposal; outreach does not establish an agreement.

Cromemco is a moderate CP/M/FlexiBUS prospect but a weak Logix-video prospect because of its independent OS and graphics strategy. Altos is a moderately strong CP/M prospect with moderate FlexiBUS and limited video potential. Intertec has moderately strong CP/M and moderate host-specific FlexiBUS potential; schedule late-1979 evaluation and possible 1980 qualification. Heath/Heathkit is a moderate CP/M/FlexiBUS prospect for later feasibility work. Neither implies a June release or a host redesign.

Seek independent implementations in printers, disks, communications, input, instruments and specialist output. Match opportunities to vendor-owned product variants rather than relabelling every existing device. Printing needs explicit character/status and paper handling; plotting and specialist functions need their own profiles, while disks need geometry, durable writes, boot and recovery rules. Native faster disk interfaces remain valid.

marketing_steps.description: Publish separate compatibility profiles and update them for the June offerings.

marketing_presentation.description: Publish {cpm} host/CPU, memory and adapter requirements alongside DRI’s portable-extension release. Ordinary CP/M remains usable without TUI or FlexiBUS; extended services and application binaries require named supported configurations. Explain {tui} as shared interaction and {c} as source-level contracts with separate target builds. The Apple II/S-100 profiles and AION C 2.0 arrive at the June launch; later ERA and pointer capabilities are outside this release.

Publish {bus} electrical/transport rules, host drivers, device classes and diagnostics independently of CP/M and video. One device connects to each point-to-point port; passive hubs and daisy chains are unsupported, and the faster rate is at most {rate} KB/s before overhead. Distinguish the C display API, video controller and {video} monitor connection. Eighty columns require a qualified 640-pixel monitor; a consumer TV or existing 320-pixel monitor does not become compatible through a cable.

Provide {sdk}, published versions, reference-driver access, conformance tests, configuration diagnostics and a certification dispute process. State non-exclusive own-brand implementation and component-access principles, supply priorities and manufacturer participation. Settle reference-code rights, CP/M licensing, support duration/staffing, maintenance funding, governance, certification scope, allocations and warranties before firm offers. Preserve each supplier’s ownership, branding and specialist support.

marketing_steps.description: Qualify the demonstrations, supplier contributions and public disclosure.

marketing_presentation.description: Rehearse named configurations with supplier workshops and record failures and corrections. Test the Aurelia/Model II document round trip separately from Aurelia compilation, FlexiDisk II Apple-format writing and Apple II execution. Measure memory/workspace, disk formats, loading/recalculation, UI redraw and peripheral behaviour; test ROM-bank restoration across display/disk calls. Book suitable space and audiovisual equipment, secure participant clearance and label prepared data or recordings.

Keep the Model II demonstration labelled prototype until its release. AION supplies the June cards; SMC is a future source subject to chip qualification. Apple’s participation concerns native Apple products, not S-100 endorsement. Separate shipping products, qualified demonstrations, prototypes and recruitment prospects; manufacturer interest, forecasts and targets are not sales or commitments.

Until {reveal}, describe the new architecture only as next-generation computers. Withhold product/processor/OS names, word size, ISA/registers, memory organization, clocks, performance figures, chip counts, schematics, board images, bus topology, future displays and coprocessor internals. Apply this to talks, Q&A, press, dealers, OEMs and attachments. Current CP/M/FlexiBUS/video documentation and the released Apple 6502 target are public. Answer architecture questions with the NCC 1980 disclosure plan; make no unspecified support-duration, withdrawal or engineering guarantee.

marketing_steps.description: Present cross-platform C development, familiar interfaces and the independent ecosystem.

marketing_presentation.description: The presentation lasts {programme_minutes} minutes, followed by questions. Show current products first and label the supplier roadmap separately.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Open with independent choice: shared application interfaces, documents and peripherals let customers keep useful work while changing computer brands. Introduce the software, bus and display standards as independently adoptable.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. DRI explains the portable CP/M extensions. Demonstrate an Abacus document round trip between Aurelia and the {model} prototype using separately qualified editions and an explicit transfer path. Show the {option} as a prototype; its recorded release is {release}, not the NCC date.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Feature {ledger} as an independent C-application pioneer. SSG demonstrates its native Z80 AION C implementation, ROM TUI forms and versioned balance exports to Abacus, explaining the benefit of shared editing and controls while retaining its accounting rules, ownership and support. This is General Ledger, not a larger accounting suite, a Model II port or a newly released Apple edition. Show how {basic} also uses shared TUI services without describing BASIC as a C port.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Operate a qualified FlexiBUS peripheral sequentially on named hosts. Show identification, supported class functions and driver requirements, attaching only with the port quiescent. Introduce the Apple II Expansion Card, S-100 FlexiBUS Interface and dual-format FlexiDisk II as separate choices.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Present {apple_video} and {s100_video} with ROM-backed TUI and callable libraries. On matching qualified monitors, demonstrate the full June 1979 Aurelia control behaviour and text/bitmap/sprite modes: frames, windows, editing, selection and redraw. Apple uses native 6502 code; S-100 TUI requires qualified CP/M/TUI extensions. Explain keyboard-command mappings and independent host performance. Preserve native Apple graphics/sound access; no automatic conversion of legacy graphics or later mouse/professional modes is implied.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Launch {compiler}: edit and compile a small shared C sample on Aurelia, save the native 6502 executable on an Apple DOS 3.2-compatible disk using {disk}, move the disk to Apple II and run it under its existing DOS installation. A compatible Disk II reader needs no Logix interface merely to read the disk; directly connecting FlexiDisk II to Apple does. Rebuild common TUI/drawing calls for Logix video, then show separately named native Apple graphics and speaker functions. The IDE stays on Aurelia; CPU-specific assembly and direct hardware access still need adapters. An Apple representative joins this native Apple demonstration without endorsing S-100 systems.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Give independent hardware pioneers a dedicated roadmap segment. Use {bridge} and {printer} to explain vendor-owned FlexiBUS bridge/native-interface approaches, and {leedex} and {sanyo} to explain purpose-built digital-input monitor variants. These are candidate paths in June, not shipping products or confirmed stage participants: the recorded estimated releases are {bridge_date}, {printer_date}, {leedex_date} and {sanyo_date}, respectively. Native Centronics printers remain behind a bridge; existing composite monitors do not become digital through a cable. Describe only tested raster/readability profiles, without promising 80 columns on every monitor. Invite supplier representatives only once participation and claims are cleared.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. {presenter} explains that shared C logic and documented APIs reduce migration work, while target-specific builds, data-format validation and testing remain necessary. Future computers will not execute Z80 binaries natively; describe the planned optional Z80 compatibility path without revealing its implementation. Continue CP/M tools and maintenance alongside future development; eight-bit systems retain business, home and education roles without a fixed replacement date.

Allow {duration_minutes} minutes. Close with available products, prototype demonstrations and prospective supplier programmes clearly distinguished. Direct customers to dealer demonstrations and developers to the SDK, compatibility directory, migration clinics and implementation programme.

marketing_steps.description: Run dealer demonstrations, trade-press activity and developer clinics.

marketing_presentation.description: Reuse the NCC demonstrations and compatibility guides rather than repeat the keynote. Teach C target adapters, console/file portability, the Apple disk-transfer workflow, ROM TUI bindings and device-class drivers. Publish named supported configurations, application editions, test failures and support contacts; distinguish shipping products, prototypes and qualification work.

Refresh the pioneer directory as products become available. The Model II CP/M/FlexiBUS release is {tandy_date}; the {bridge} has an estimated {bridge_date} release. Later printer and monitor candidates stay on the roadmap until their own dates and qualification evidence. Suppliers retain their own brands, licences, sales and support.

marketing_steps.description: Review adoption targets and the evidence behind ecosystem growth.

marketing_presentation.description: By end-1979, target Tandy shipping, one additional OEM selling a supported CP/M-extension or FlexiBUS configuration, another in qualification and verified devices in several categories. By NCC 1980, target {manufacturers} distinct non-Logix manufacturers. Count Tandy once; exclude duplicate dealer builds and SKUs. These are goals, not achieved totals.

Track compatible-computer sell-through, qualified C and other application editions, peripheral shipments/classes, document interchange, support incidents, supplier concentration and component availability. Compare each pioneer’s actual scope and release date with the directory; separate application use of an API, bus implementation and digital-monitor compatibility. Do not turn adoption assumptions into measured sales.

marketing_steps.description: Publish customer evidence and prepare the next campaign.

marketing_presentation.description: Assemble verified customer examples, compatibility results and supplier configurations. Report progress and unresolved access/support issues, keeping future releases and NCC 1980 targets separate from results. The {printer} is recorded only to {release_month}; do not infer shipment by this January review from month precision alone. Leedex and Sanyo digital variants remain later roadmap items. Maintain the architecture embargo until the announced reveal.

before.title: NCC 1979 open architecture and migration campaign — execution
before.description: Prepare the compatibility programme and partner demonstrations, deliver the NCC 1979 presentation and expansion-product launch, then run recruitment, dealer activity and qualification follow-up through the January 1980 review. Campaign.ncc1979 supplies the messages, presentation and marketing materials.

inputs.description: The Aurelia launch provides the working platform and business applications used to prepare cross-vendor demonstrations.
The Tandy cooperation agreement provides the basis for the Model II prototype and application-interchange work.
The limited Apple cooperation agreement provides documentation, test machines and compatibility assistance for native Apple II products.

Prepare named configurations, host-specific drivers, documented transfer paths and measured resource limits. Protect future architecture information and clear partner participation before public demonstrations.

outcomes.description: Published compatibility profiles, implementation guidance and records of unresolved access and support terms.
Rehearsed demonstration configurations, interoperability test records and an issue register distinguishing verified behaviour from limitations.
The NCC presentation and expansion-product launch have been delivered, with native Apple and S-100 support described separately and partner responsibilities retained.

An updated compatibility directory, recruitment and qualification records, dealer and developer materials, and an evidence-based closing review. Adoption and sales targets are not treated as achieved outcomes.

steps.description: Evaluate recruitment prospects and engineering kits. Prioritise North Star, with Lifeboat as a possible integration or distribution partner, then Vector Graphic. Preserve existing applications and display investment; interest does not constitute an agreement.

Treat North Star and Vector as strong CP/M prospects with moderately strong FlexiBUS prospects; optional Logix video is a moderate fit for North Star and a lower fit for Vector. Cromemco is a moderate CP/M and FlexiBUS prospect but a weak Logix-video prospect because of its own OS and graphics strategy. Altos is a moderately strong CP/M prospect with moderate FlexiBUS and limited Logix-video potential; no platform redesign is assumed. Intertec has moderately strong CP/M and moderate host-specific FlexiBUS potential, with limited Logix-video interest; plan late-1979 evaluation and possible 1980 qualification, not June availability. Heath/Heathkit has moderate CP/M and host-specific FlexiBUS potential but limited Logix-video interest; treat it as later feasibility work, not a promised 1979 release. These assessments guide outreach and do not establish commitments.
Publish compatibility profiles and provide reference-driver and test access alongside the separate DRI extension release. Record unresolved commercial and support terms.

Prepare the presentation space, audiovisual equipment and qualified demonstration systems. Test document round trips, disk formats, memory limits, loading, recalculation and device behaviour. Review all public material for the embargo and secure partner clearance.
Run supplier workshops, test named configurations and record failures and required corrections before public demonstrations.
Deliver the NCC presentation and the combined Apple II/S-100 expansion-product launch using the approved campaign materials and qualified systems.
Run dealer demonstrations, joint trade-press activity and developer clinics. Maintain a directory that distinguishes shipping, qualified and prototype configurations.
Review progress against the campaign’s adoption targets using verified OEM configurations, qualifications and third-party device availability.

Track compatible-computer sell-through across vendors, qualified application editions, peripheral shipments and supported device classes, document-interchange results, support incidents, supplier concentration and component availability. Count distinct manufacturers rather than duplicate dealer builds or SKUs.

Prepare the closing review with verified customer examples, compatibility results and partner configurations. Report progress toward NCC 1980 goals without claiming unverified results or disclosing future architecture.
